description: Device Tracking Integration: Wire existing device tracking utilities (lib/device-id.ts, lib/middleware/device-tracking.ts) into Better Auth login flow. Create device verification UI page and authenticated fetch wrapper to inject device headers on all requests. Existing APIs app/api/auth/verify-device and app/api/auth/request-device-otp are ready.
steps: 1. Create lib/auth/track-device.ts with trackDeviceLogin(userId, deviceId, deviceName) function: Call trackDevice(userId) from lib/middleware/device-tracking.ts, if isNewDevice === true generate 6-digit OTP (Math.floor(100000 + Math.random() * 900000)), hash with crypto.createHash('sha256'), store in verifications table with identifier 'device-verify:${deviceId}', call sendNewDeviceAlertEmail(userId, deviceName, otp) using lib/email.ts.

2. Modify lib/auth-config.ts to add hooks.after.signIn callback: Read deviceId and deviceName from request.headers.get('x-device-id') and get('x-device-name'), call trackDeviceLogin(), return result. Note: Better Auth hooks signature may differ, verify in Better Auth 1.7.7 docs.

3. Create lib/utils/authenticated-fetch.ts: Wrap fetch() to auto-inject headers. Import getOrCreateDeviceId() and getDeviceName() from lib/device-id.ts, add X-Device-ID and X-Device-Name to all requests.

4. Create app/doctor/verify-device/page.tsx: Form with single input for 6-digit OTP, read deviceId from URL query params, on submit POST to /api/auth/verify-device with { deviceId, otp }, on success redirect to /doctor, on error show 'Invalid OTP' message.
5. Update doctor login flow: After successful login in app/login/page.tsx, check if response includes requiresDeviceVerification flag, if true redirect to /doctor/verify-device?deviceId=${deviceId}.
6. Replace all fetch() calls in app/doctor/page.tsx and app/doctor/bookings/page.tsx with authenticatedFetch() from lib/utils/authenticated-fetch.ts to ensure device headers are sent.

7. Test new device flow: Clear localStorage, login as doctor, verify OTP email received, enter OTP on /doctor/verify-device, confirm redirected to /doctor. Test known device: Login again from same browser, no OTP prompt.
acceptance_criteria: Login from new device (cleared localStorage) triggers email with 6-digit OTP
Device verification page /doctor/verify-device accepts valid OTP and marks device as trusted in userDevices table
Login from known device skips OTP flow entirely
Invalid OTP shows error message and allows retry up to 3 attempts (rate limiting in existing API)
All authenticated API calls from doctor pages include X-Device-ID and X-Device-Name headers
userDevices table has new record after first login from device with trusted = false, trusted = true after OTP verification
verification: Open Chrome DevTools → Application → Local Storage → Clear medcin_device_id key
Go to http://localhost:3000/login and sign in as provisioned doctor
Check email inbox for 'New device login' alert with 6-digit OTP
Enter correct OTP → redirected to /doctor dashboard
Check database: SELECT * FROM user_devices WHERE user_id = 'doctor_user_id' → record exists with trusted = true
Logout and login again → No OTP prompt, goes straight to dashboard
Check Chrome DevTools Network tab on /doctor page → Request headers include X-Device-ID and X-Device-Name
